_note: v2 hook overrides for the boulangerie. In v1 every verb was 'Monsieur Verbe'; in the v2 paintings each verb is a different person, so those hooks name who is painted. Other overrides match painted counts/details. v1 data is untouched.

fr_compter_verb.hook: The shopkeeper COUNTS on her fingers, one, two, three, next to the bowl of coins. Compter is COUNT with a French ending, and the p stays quiet.
fr_compter_verb.why: Painted as the shopkeeper, not Monsieur Verbe.

fr_vendre_verb.hook: The shop assistant SELLS a fresh baguette across the counter. Think of English VEND (to sell, as in a vending machine): vend, vendre.
fr_vendre_verb.why: Painted as the assistant, not Monsieur Verbe.

fr_payer_verb.hook: A customer PAYS with a big gold coin and punches the air: PAY... YAY!
fr_payer_verb.why: Painted as a customer, not Monsieur Verbe.

fr_choisir_verb.hook: A girl in a yellow dress taps her chin and CHOOSES a treat in the display case. CHOisir starts like CHOose: cho-, choose.
fr_choisir_verb.why: Painted as a girl, not Monsieur Verbe.

fr_petrir_verb.hook: An apprentice girl KNEADS the dough in a giant PETRI dish: pay-TREER = petri.
fr_petrir_verb.why: Painted as an apprentice, not Monsieur Verbe.

fr_melanger_verb.hook: An apprentice boy MIXES the batter inside half a water-MELON: MAY-lahn = melon.
fr_melanger_verb.why: Painted as an apprentice, not Monsieur Verbe.

fr_cuire_verb.hook: A young baker in a CHOIR-boy collar sings "O!" while he COOKS a pancake: KWEER = choir.
fr_cuire_verb.why: Painted as a young baker, not Monsieur Verbe.

fr_baguette_noun.hook: A proud grey cat stands on top of her tower of BAGUETTES.
fr_baguette_noun.why: The painting shows four baguettes, not five.

fr_sac_noun.hook: A brown paper SACK stuffed with baguettes. Sac sounds just like SACK.
fr_sac_noun.why: The painting shows two baguettes, not three.

fr_panier_noun.hook: A wicker PANNIER full of baguettes on the back of a little bike. A pannier is a basket bag: pannier, panier (pah-NYAY).

fr_plateau_noun.hook: Beside the oven, the baking TRAY sits on the flat top of a little rocky PLATEAU: plah-TOH = plateau.
fr_plateau_noun.why: Painted as a tray resting on a small mesa.

fr_seau_noun.hook: The leaky BUCKET has been SEWN up with big red stitches: SOH = sew.
fr_seau_noun.why: The stitches are painted; the needle is not clearly visible.

fr_tablier_noun.hook: A little TABLE wears an APRON with a smiling face and kicks up a leg: "TABLE, YAY!" = tah-blee-YAY.
fr_tablier_noun.why: Matches the painted apron-table (the bucket rides on top of it).

fr_boite_noun.hook: The cake BOX has a sail and floats on a puddle like a BOAT: BWAHT = boat.
fr_boite_noun.why: Painted on a puddle on the workbench.
